issues.main_description_html:
Projects left is_complete = false for more than 24 hours after creation should be automatically soft-deleted, checked hourly.

Design

  • Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-22-cleanup-incomplete-projects-design.md
  • Plan: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-22-cleanup-incomplete-projects.md

Implementation

In-process time.Ticker goroutine started from cmd/api, checking once on boot then hourly. Reuses a DeleteProject function extracted from the existing Delete HTTP handler so both paths share one soft-delete code path. Disable via CLEANUP_INCOMPLETE_PROJECTS_ENABLED=false.

PR: #98

RESULT

Implemented across 4 commits on feature/cleanup-incomplete-projects (branch pushed, PR #98 open against development):

  • 1ac391c feat(jobs): add pure eligibility check for incomplete-project cleanup
  • f7f5985 feat(jobs): add hourly incomplete-project cleanup loop

issues.display_title: Issue #101: Require auth for GET /v1/floorplan/:id on unpublished projects
issues.main_description_html:
RESULT 23/07/26

✅ Implementation: Floorplan Draft Auth (Issue #101 / PR #107)

Overview

GET /v1/floorplan/:id now keeps published floorplans public while protecting draft and unpublished floorplans behind project membership.

This fixes the security gap where anyone with a project UUID could read full floorplan data for an unpublished project.

Behavior

  • Published project: public 200, no token required.
  • Draft or unpublished project: requires Authorization: Bearer <token>.
  • Draft or unpublished project with viewer, editor, or owner role: 200.
  • Draft or unpublished project with anonymous, invalid token, missing user, or non-member: 404.
  • Unknown project: same 404 response body as unauthorized draft access.

The endpoint path did not change:

GET /v1/floorplan/:id

Files Changed

  • src/action/v1/floorplan/get.go
  • src/action/v1/floorplan/get_test.go
  • src/middleware/auth.go
  • src/middleware/auth_test.go
  • src/routes/v1/floorplan.go
  • go.mod
  • go.sum

Access Control Implementation

src/action/v1/floorplan/get.go now:

  1. Validates :id as a UUID.
  2. Loads the project by ID.
  3. Returns 404 when the project does not exist.
  4. Allows public access when project.Status == "published".
  5. For all other statuses, resolves the optional bearer user.
  6. Calls members.FetchRole(user.UniqueID, projectID).
  7. Allows viewer, editor, and owner.
  8. Returns the same 404 body for anonymous and non-member access.

The existing buildFloorplanResponse(project) serializer is still used, so response shape and object-storage URL rewriting are unchanged.

Optional Auth Helper

src/middleware/auth.go now exposes:

func OptionalUser(c *fiber.Ctx) (*models.User, bool, error)

It uses the same Authorization: Bearer <token> source as middleware.Auth(), but does not reject anonymous requests.

Return behavior:

  • Missing token: ok=false
  • Invalid or expired token: ok=false
  • Valid token but missing user row: ok=false
  • Valid token with database error: returns error
  • Valid token and user row: returns user with ok=true

The existing middleware.Auth() behavior is unchanged.

Tests

Added endpoint matrix coverage in src/action/v1/floorplan/get_test.go:

  • anonymous + draft: 404
  • non-member + draft: 404
  • viewer + draft: 200
  • editor + draft: 200
  • owner + draft: 200
  • anonymous + published: 200
  • unknown UUID response matches unauthorized draft body

Added optional auth tests in src/middleware/auth_test.go:

  • missing token returns anonymous
  • invalid token returns anonymous
  • valid token works with nil DB fallback
  • valid token with missing DB user returns anonymous
  • valid token with DB error returns error

Review Feedback Fixes

PR review flagged two minor issues:

  1. Unused sqlite modules from the first test attempt.

    • Fixed with go mod tidy.
    • Removed gorm.io/driver/sqlite and github.com/mattn/go-sqlite3.
    • Kept github.com/glebarez/sqlite, which works without CGO and is used by tests.

  2. OptionalUser returned an error value but never used it.

    • Fixed by returning real DB errors while treating gorm.ErrRecordNotFound as anonymous.
    • This makes the 500 branch in floorplan.Get reachable for real auth DB failures.

Verification

Passed:

go test ./src/middleware ./src/action/v1/floorplan ./src/routes/v1 -count=1
go build ./...

Full suite:

go test ./... -count=1

Still fails on pre-existing unrelated tests:

  • src/action/v1/predict: TestPredictStreamsSSEEvents
  • src/services: TestSendPasswordResetEmailUsesSeparateTemplate

Deployment Note

Frontend draft editor and preview code must send the bearer token before this backend change is deployed. Otherwise draft floorplan loads will return 404 for authenticated users whose request does not include the token.

Frontend coordination is tracked in GoThruMedia/gothru-3d-floormap#358.

Sprint #100 / PRD gothru-3d-floormap#349. Priority: P0 — security.

Description

GET /v1/floorplan/:id (src/action/v1/floorplan/get.go) is registered without auth middleware and performs no published check — anyone holding a project UUID can read full floorplan data of a draft project. The route comment claims GET is public because published floorplans are viewed on /preview, but the published-only public endpoint is GET /v1/live/:key (#85); this endpoint serves everything.

Why

Server-side role enforcement (PRD #349 DoD) is meaningless for reads while an unauthenticated endpoint serves any project. Viewer/editor/owner gating starts here.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Published project → GET stays public (current /preview behavior unchanged)
  • Unpublished project → requires auth and FetchRole != RoleNone; otherwise 404 (identical body for unknown vs unauthorized, matching the #85 pattern)
  • Tests: anonymous+draft → 404, non-member+draft → 404, viewer/editor/owner+draft → 200, anonymous+published → 200
  • Build + existing tests green

Dependencies

None

issues.display_title: Issue #102: Add role enforcement test matrix for project write endpoints
issues.main_description_html:
RESULT 23/07/26

✅ Implementation: Role Enforcement Test Matrix (Issue #102 / PR #108 )

Overview

Added endpoint-level tests that prove project write permissions are enforced for viewer, editor, owner, and non-member users.

The tests caught three endpoints that were still owner-only by direct project.UserID comparison instead of using the shared role helper. Those endpoints now use members.FetchRole(...).CanWrite().

Files Changed

  • src/routes/v1/role_matrix_test.go
  • src/action/v1/project/delete.go
  • src/action/v1/project/publish.go
  • src/action/v1/project/unpublish.go

Test Coverage

Added matrix coverage for project write endpoints:

  • PATCH /v1/projects/:id
  • DELETE /v1/projects/:id
  • POST /v1/projects/:id/publish
  • POST /v1/projects/:id/unpublish
  • POST /v1/projects/:id/file
  • DELETE /v1/projects/:id/file
  • POST /v1/floorplan/:id

Expected roles:

  • viewer: 403
  • editor: success
  • owner: success
  • non-member: 403

Added matrix coverage for member-management endpoints:

  • POST /v1/projects/:id/members
  • PATCH /v1/projects/:id/members/:userId
  • DELETE /v1/projects/:id/members/:userId

Expected roles:

  • viewer: 403
  • editor: 403
  • owner: success
  • non-member: 403

Self-Removal Note

Member self-removal is currently owner-only. This is intentional and matches PRD open question 4: self-removal is not implemented in this task.

The test TestMemberSelfRemovalCurrentlyOwnerOnly documents this behavior:

  • viewer deleting their own membership row: 403

Authorization Fixes

The matrix exposed three endpoints that still checked ownership directly:

  • DELETE /v1/projects/:id
  • POST /v1/projects/:id/publish
  • POST /v1/projects/:id/unpublish

Those handlers now call:

role, err := members.FetchRole(user.UniqueID, id)
if err != nil {
    return helpers.FormatResponse(c, 500, fiber.Map{"error": "database error"}, startTime)
}
if !role.CanWrite() {
    return helpers.FormatResponse(c, 403, fiber.Map{"error": "forbidden"}, startTime)
}

This aligns them with the existing role model:

  • owner can write
  • editor can write
  • viewer cannot write
  • non-member cannot write

Test Design

The test uses a real Fiber router and in-memory SQLite database via github.com/glebarez/sqlite.

Each subtest creates isolated data:

  • owner user
  • editor user
  • viewer user
  • non-member user
  • target user for member invite/update/delete paths
  • project owned by owner
  • editor and viewer project_members rows
  • seeded project file for delete-file tests

Requests use real bearer tokens generated with utils.GenerateSessionToken, so the route-level middleware.Auth() path is exercised.

Verification

Passed:

go test ./src/routes/v1 -run RoleMatrix -count=1
go test ./src/routes/v1 ./src/action/v1/project ./src/action/v1/files ./src/action/v1/floorplan ./src/action/v1/members -count=1
go build ./...

Full suite:

go test ./... -count=1

Still fails on pre-existing unrelated tests:

  • src/action/v1/predict: TestPredictStreamsSSEEvents
  • src/services: TestSendPasswordResetEmailUsesSeparateTemplate

Sprint #100 / PRD gothru-3d-floormap#349.

Description

Role gating is already wired through FetchRole/CanWrite/CanManageMembers (src/action/v1/members/role.go) on every routed project-scoped write endpoint, but the only test is role_test.go (pure decideRole). Add an endpoint-level matrix proving each gate: viewer → 403, editor → 200, owner → 200 (members management: editor → 403).

Endpoints: PATCH /projects/:id, DELETE /projects/:id, POST /projects/:id/publish, POST /projects/:id/unpublish, POST/DELETE /projects/:id/file, POST /floorplan/:id, POST/PATCH/DELETE /projects/:id/members.

Why

The gates exist but nothing fails if one is dropped in a refactor. PRD #349 DoD: "Restrictions enforced server-side, verified in all three roles."

Acceptance Criteria

  • Table test per endpoint covering viewer/editor/owner (+ non-member → 403/404)
  • Documented note in this issue: member self-removal is currently owner-only (PRD open question 4 — not implemented on purpose)
  • Build + tests green

Dependencies

Dead /v1/upload removal is #77, not this task.

issues.display_title: Issue #103: Replace generic 403 "forbidden" with owner-naming messages
issues.main_description_html:
RESULT 23/07/26

✅ Implementation: Owner-Naming 403 Messages (Task #103 / PR #111 )

Overview

Every project-scoped denial returned a bare {"error": "forbidden"}. PRD #349's
Definition of Done forbids that: no message may read "forbidden" or
"unauthorised" — each one must name who can unblock the caller. This task
replaces the message everywhere and hardens the one place where downstream code
depended on the old wording.

Code Implementation

  1. The shared body builder (src/action/v1/members/forbidden.go, new):

    • forbiddenBody(ownerEmail) is the pure shape and the only place the
      sentence lives:
      {"error": "Only the project owner (owner@email) can do this", "owner_email": "..."}.
    • An empty email degrades to {"error": "Only the project owner can do this"}
      with no owner_email key — better an unnamed owner than an empty
      parenthesis or a leaked blank field.
    • ownerEmail(userID) swallows the lookup error and returns "". An
      authorization denial must never become a 500 because the owner's user row
      is missing.
    • Two entry points, matching the two shapes the call sites already had:
      • Forbidden(project models.Project) — the handler already loaded the
        project row (10 sites); costs one user lookup.
      • ForbiddenByProjectID(projectID string) — the members/ handlers hold
        only the route param; loads user_id, then delegates to Forbidden.

  2. Call sites — 13 total, all helpers.FormatResponse(c, 403, ...):

    • project/: get.go, update.go, delete.go, publish.go, unpublish.go
    • members/: create.go, update.go, delete.go, list.go
    • files/: project_get.go, project_upload.go, project_delete.go
    • floorplan/post.go, upload/upload.go

    The issue listed 12; members/list.go was the missed one and is included.

  3. Error-contract refactor (src/action/v1/shared/shared.go):

    ResolvePath returned errors.New("forbidden path traversal"), and
    files/get.go / files/delete.go picked 403-vs-400 by
    strings.Contains(err.Error(), "forbidden"). Changing the wording would have
    silently downgraded traversal attempts to 400 Invalid filename with no test
    failure — a real security regression hiding inside a copy edit.

    Fix: package-level sentinels shared.ErrForbiddenPath and
    shared.ErrInvalidFilename, matched with errors.Is at both call sites.
    This mirrors the pattern already in src/action/v1/auth/avatar.go
    (ErrForbiddenPath + errors.Is in src/controllers/v1/auth/avatar.go), so
    there is one error-contract idiom in the codebase, not two. The 403 body for
    these two file routes is now
    "Filename may not point outside your session folder".

    Note this path is not project-scoped — it is session path traversal, so it
    has no owner to name. It was in scope only because of the string coupling.

Tests

  • src/action/v1/members/forbidden_test.go — pins both branches of
    forbiddenBody: owner named with owner_email present, and unknown owner with
    owner_email absent. Pure function, no DB, matching role_test.go's style.
  • src/action/v1/shared/resolvepath_test.go — guards the error contract
    files/get.go and files/delete.go branch on, so the 403/400 split cannot
    regress the next time a message is reworded.

go build ./... and go vet ./... are clean. go test ./... passes except
src/action/v1/predict and src/services, both of which fail identically on the
pre-change baseline and are untouched by this work.

Frontend Impact — BREAKING

403 response bodies changed shape. gothru-3d-floormap must be told:

  • error is now a full sentence naming the owner, not the token "forbidden".
    Any FE code matching on the literal string will stop matching.
  • A new optional owner_email field is present when the owner is resolvable.
  • GET/DELETE on the session file routes return a different 403 body string.

Files Changed

File Change
src/action/v1/members/forbidden.go new — body builder + owner lookup
src/action/v1/members/forbidden_test.go new — body shape tests
src/action/v1/shared/shared.go sentinel errors from ResolvePath
src/action/v1/shared/resolvepath_test.go new — error contract test
src/action/v1/files/get.go, delete.go errors.Is instead of string match
13 handlers across project/, members/, files/, floorplan/, upload/ call the new builder

Sprint #100 / PRD gothru-3d-floormap#349.

Description

All project-scoped 403s return {"error": "forbidden"} — PRD #349 DoD forbids bare "forbidden"/"unauthorised"; each message must name who can help. Add one helper (e.g. in src/action/v1/members) that loads the owner's email and returns {"error": "Only the project owner (owner@email) can do this", "owner_email": "..."}, then replace the 12 call-sites in project/, members/, files/, floorplan/, upload/.

Careful: files/get.go:22 and files/delete.go:22 string-match err.Error() for "forbidden" from a shared helper — refactor that helper's error contract together with the message change, not just the strings.

Why

PRD #349 DoD: "No message reads 'forbidden' or 'unauthorised' — each one names who can help."

Acceptance Criteria

  • No project-scoped 403 response body contains bare "forbidden"
  • Response includes owner_email; message names the owner
  • files/get.go / files/delete.go error matching still works (tests)
  • FE (gothru-3d-floormap) notified: response shape changed — new owner_email field
  • Build + tests green

Dependencies

None (test matrix lands in the sibling test task)

issues.display_title: Issue #109: Refactor: reuse loaded project in role checks (drop duplicate query in FetchRole call sites)
issues.main_description_html:
Follow-up from PR #108 review (non-blocking nit).

Description

Every role-gated handler loads the project (First(&project), 404 handling), then calls members.FetchRole(userID, projectID) — which re-queries the same project row (SELECT user_id). One redundant PK query per request, on every project-scoped endpoint.

Call sites (10 after #108 merges):

  • src/action/v1/project/get.go, update.go, delete.go, publish.go, unpublish.go
  • src/action/v1/files/project_get.go, project_upload.go, project_delete.go
  • src/action/v1/floorplan/post.go
  • src/action/v1/upload/upload.go

Proposed fix

Add members.FetchRoleForProject(project models.Project, userID string) (Role, error) — runs only the member-row query and feeds the already-loaded project.UserID into the existing decideRole. Handlers that already hold the project switch to it; FetchRole stays for callers without a loaded project (Access endpoint).

Acceptance Criteria

  • No handler queries the project twice for one request
  • role_matrix_test.go still green (matrix unchanged — pure refactor, no behavior change)
  • Build + tests green

Dependencies

Do after PR #108 merges (it adds 3 of the call sites).

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

RESULT

Added members.FetchRoleForProject(project, userID) (membership query only, reuses loaded project.UserID via decideRole); FetchRole now delegates to it. Switched 11 call sites — the 10 listed plus floorplan/get.go (same double-query, found during the fix). members create/list/update/delete and Access left on FetchRole (no project row loaded before the check).

PR: #110 (stacked on #108 — merge that first). Commit: a9217d3. Build/vet green; role matrix + members tests green; full suite only pre-existing failures.

RESULT 23/07/26

✅ Implementation: Collaborator-Added Notification Email (Task #104 / PR #112 )

Overview

POST /v1/projects/:id/members added a user to a project silently — the invitee
learned about it only by opening the app. This task sends them a Plunk email
naming the inviter, the project and the granted role.

Code Implementation

  1. Template constant (src/config/templates.go):

    TemplateCollabAdded = "7cb4b211-31c4-460a-b3b2-8a45eabd998e" follows the
    existing hardcoded-ID pattern (no new env var).

  2. Service method (src/services/email.go):

    SendCollaboratorAddedEmail(toEmail, name, inviterName, projectName, role, link)
    triggers the template with fullname, email, inviter, project_name,
    role and url. inviterName is included so the recipient can tell an
    expected invite from a stray one. The collabTpl field is wired in
    NewEmailService alongside verifyTpl / resetTpl.

  3. Handler wiring (src/action/v1/members/create.go):

    After the member upsert succeeds, go emailService.SendCollaboratorAddedEmail(...)
    — fire-and-forget, matching auth/forgotPassword.go:36. A bounced email can
    never fail an invite that is already committed. The package now owns a
    var emailService = services.NewEmailService(), mirroring
    auth/shared.go:47.

    The project row was loaded with Select("user_id"); it now also selects
    name, so the email copy gets the project name without a second query.

    Link: FRONTEND_URL + /editor/<projectID>, matching the fmt.Sprintf style
    used by the verify and reset links. The FE route is editor/[projectId] —
    there is no /project/[id] page, so that path would 404 (PR #112 review).

  4. Stale comment fixed (src/services/email.go):

    NewEmailService's doc claimed template IDs come from PLUNK_VERIFY_TEMPLATE
    / PLUNK_RESET_TEMPLATE. Those env vars do not exist anywhere in the
    codebase — the IDs are constants in config/templates.go. The comment now
    documents only what is actually read from the environment
    (USEPLUNK_SECRET_KEY, USEPLUNK_URL); it also drops the false claim that
    USEPLUNK_URL is optional with a default, since trigger returns an error
    when it is empty.

  5. Password-reset payload bug, found while extending the tests:

    TestSendPasswordResetEmailUsesSeparateTemplate asserted data["email"], but
    SendPasswordResetEmail never sent that key — the test was failing on the
    pre-change baseline. Root cause is the missing field, not the assertion, so
    "email": toEmail was added to the reset payload, consistent with the
    verification email. src/services is green again.

Tests

src/services/email_test.go gains TestSendCollaboratorAddedEmail, using the
existing newCaptureServer sink: it asserts the template ID, the recipient, and
every one of the six data fields the template copy renders.

go build ./... and go vet ./... are clean. go test ./... passes except
src/action/v1/predict, which fails identically on the pre-change baseline and
is unrelated to this work.

Plunk template

Created in the Plunk dashboard, ID 7cb4b211-31c4-460a-b3b2-8a45eabd998e.

  • Subject: "You've been added to a project on MapThru" — deliberately free of
    variables, since the inviter, project and role all appear in the first line of
    the body.
  • Variables rendered: {{fullname}}, {{inviter}}, {{project_name}},
    {{role}}, {{url}}. {{email}} is also sent but unused in the copy.

Delivery was verified live against the real Plunk endpoint on 2026-07-23: two
sends to pebisandi04@gmail.com returned HTTP 200 / success: true (email IDs
40ba7187-6540-4ff9-a06d-503fc74e8ec5 and
5d2a35e7-e54a-4276-90e4-db1caaa76c6c), confirming the template ID resolves and
Plunk accepts the payload.

Those sends hit the template directly with hand-written data, and a 200 only
means Plunk queued the message. Two things remain unverified by anything in this
repo: that the rendered email shows every variable rather than raw {{...}}
placeholders, and that the full path works — invite a registered user through
POST /v1/projects/:id/members and confirm the email lands.

Files Changed

File Change
src/config/templates.go TemplateCollabAdded const
src/services/email.go new send method, collabTpl field, corrected doc comment, reset payload email field
src/services/email_test.go new test for the collaborator email
src/action/v1/members/create.go async send after upsert, selects project name, /editor/<id> CTA link

Sprint #100 / PRD gothru-3d-floormap#349.

Description

When POST /v1/projects/:id/members adds a registered user, send them a notification email through the existing Plunk service (src/services/email.go).

  • New template created in the Plunk dashboard ("X added you to project Y as {role}" + project link) — needs Plunk dashboard access
  • New const TemplateCollabAdded in src/config/templates.go (follow the existing hardcoded-ID pattern — no new env var)
  • New SendCollaboratorAddedEmail(toEmail, name, projectName, role, link) on EmailService
  • Fire-and-forget from members/create.go after a successful upsert (go emailService.Send..., same pattern as forgotPassword.go:36)
  • Cleanup: the doc comment on NewEmailService claims template IDs come from PLUNK_VERIFY_TEMPLATE/PLUNK_RESET_TEMPLATE env vars — they don't (they come from config/templates.go). Fix the comment.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Inviting a registered user sends the email
  • Email failure does not fail the invite (async)
  • Stale env-var comment in email.go corrected
  • Build + tests green (extend email_test.go sink pattern)

Dependencies

Plunk dashboard access for template creation.
